pl-l2d38c2-d1e108.summary: States that one who sets charity as his end sets God; so Christ is the end of the law unto justice for believers, since, as Augustine's Prosper sentences say, in Christ the law is fulfilled, not consumed; all perfection is from him, beyond whom hope cannot extend; reaching him, the runner has nowhere further but somewhere to remain. The right and supreme end is God, Father, Son, and Spirit, not three ends but one, as not three gods but one.
claims: Christ is the end of the law.

pl-l2d38c2.summary: One who makes charity his end makes God his end; so Christ is the end of the law unto justice for every believer (Rom 10:4), since in him the law is fulfilled, not consumed, and beyond him hope has nowhere to reach; reaching him, the runner has nowhere further to go but somewhere to remain. The right and supreme end is God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, not three ends but one, as they are one God.
claims: To make charity one's end is to make God one's end.
Christ is the end of the law, fulfilling it.
Christ is the end in which the faithful remain.
The Trinity is one supreme end, not three.
